title: Ya-Sin 36:57-60 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ya-Sin 36:57-60 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 33. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌۭ وَلَهُم مَّا يَدَّعُونَ (٥٧) سَلَٰمٌۭ قَوْلًۭا مِّن رَّبٍّۢ رَّحِيمٍۢ (٥٨) وَٱمْتَٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ (٥٩) ۞ أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يَٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ (٦٠)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request [or wish]
[And] "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.
[Then He will say], "But stand apart today, you criminals.
Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, he is to you a clear enemy -

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Idgham with ghunnah, then without ghunnah
Idgham without ghunnah: tanween into ر
Idgham without ghunnah: noon into ل

questions.q: Chunk and link Ya-Sin 36:57-60 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 36:57-60 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 36:57-60 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find the waqf sign in 36:60 and say what it allows.
Why is Shaytan called 'a clear enemy' (36:60)?
questions.a: He openly declared his enmity to Adam and his children; his aim is to mislead.

questions.q: What covenant does Allah remind the children of Adam of (36:60)?
Ya-Sin 36:60: «أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يَٰبَنِىٓ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: 'Peace: a word from a Merciful Lord' (36:58). What would it mean to you to be greeted with salam by Allah?
questions.a: The greatest honour and comfort: it is why we spread salam now.
